definition: A tendency for evaluators to favor responses based on their order or position when comparing multiple candidates, rather than purely on content quality.
details: Position bias is a known issue in pairwise comparison evaluations (including LLM-as-a-judge setups), where simply swapping the order of two candidate responses can change which one is judged as better, motivating techniques like order randomization.
story: Picture a parachute packed by a second pair of hands: nobody plans to need it, but everyone is glad it was checked. The idea is simple: before something powerful is let loose, someone checks that it will not do real harm to real people. It is the habit of asking, before every launch, what could go wrong — and then doing something about it. Caution is not the enemy of progress — it is the reason progress gets to keep going. And that is Position Bias (in evaluation) — the reason we can move fast without breaking things, or people.
